item: Row 393 (R816): the R801 restored-key marker covers every signing key a restore places
summary: R801 wrote the restored-key marker only beside the evidence key, so a custody or annotation key pair carried in a backup from another computer read as this installation's own (in GET /api/custody/{item}/verify and in POST /api/custody/verify). The restore now writes the marker beside each custody and annotation Ed25519 key it places, BEFORE placing the pair and under restored_marker_lock (the lock the signer now also makes its own key under), after looking again for a key of this installation's under that lock (one found wins: its names kept_local, the rest not placed as raced). A marker that cannot be written places no pair: both halves are listed not placed with the reason (new string x12), fail closed. A pair that fails or races takes back the marker this call wrote, only while it is still that file. HybridSigner drops the marker when it makes a NEW Ed25519 key, under the same lock, as load_or_create_signing_key does; loading an existing key keeps it. POST /verify (describe_export local_restored) calls no signer this installation's while the custody key has its marker (verdict signatures-valid-signer-not-yours with a note); GET verify already asked through evidence.is_this_installations_key, whose marker read fails closed. APP_KEY_NAMES gains the custody and annotations markers, so an erase destroys them and still judges a keys folder holding them as the app's (lane D told). No retro-marking: a key restored from another computer by an earlier build still reads as this installation's own (release line). Stored values unchanged (R755).
